solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bear left, with New York to the west — this part?

definitions.text: Bear left, with New York to the west — this part?

parts.note: to brook something is to bear or tolerate it
L is the standard abbreviation for left

indicators.note: in an across entry west is leftward, so these letters are written right to left

parts.note: NY is the usual abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: Directions for a bear: head left, with New York lying westward — is this the neighbourhood?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the question asks which part of New York the letters build, and the answer is that borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Brooklyn is one of the five boroughs that make up New York City, so it is a part of it.

clue.text: About to adopt unfashionable course

indicators.note: adopting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning
something out is no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: Someone is about to take up a course of study that is out of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a way or path taken, which is one meaning of course.

clue.text: Sour old company porter's English language dull and verbose?

parts.note: milk that has gone off has turned sour
ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British company, now defunct
porter is a dark beer, an ale, and the 's adds the S
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A grumpy porter at a former firm finds English dull and long-winded.
explanation.walkthrough: Porter looks like a person who carries bags; here it is the dark beer, a kind of ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Officialese is the stilted, wordy jargon of bureaucrats, a dull and verbose kind of language.

clue.text: Prank with egg is bloomer

parts.note: a lark is a bit of fun or a prank
to egg someone on is to spur them

explanation.surface: A practical joke involving an egg turns out to be a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer suggests a mistake, and egg suggests something to eat; here a bloomer is something that blooms, and egg is the verb as in egg on.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a flowering garden plant, and any plant that flowers can whimsically be called a bloomer.

clue.text: A nightdress seen poorly with this?

definitions.text: A nightdress seen poorly with this?

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly, so these letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: all the letters of these three words are used

explanation.surface: Someone peering at a nightdress can barely make it out — what is the cause?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: a short-sighted person would see the garment poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-sightedness is myopia, the condition in which distant things are seen blurred.

clue.text: Holiday abroad perhaps is cure when restless

indicators.note: restless means unable to keep still, so these letters move around

parts.note: the letters of both words are used

explanation.surface: Going on holiday overseas is the remedy when you feel unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: a cruise is one kind of holiday, often abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruise is a pleasure voyage, a typical example of a vacation taken overseas.

clue.text: Charlie, going further back, becoming more distant

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
something older goes further back in time

explanation.surface: Charlie, retreating further, is growing more remote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going further back' sounds like retreating, but it means of greater age.
explanation.definitionFit: In a guessing game you are colder when further from the target, and a colder manner is more aloof.

clue.text: Vase you might pick up to bring home

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so the sound of the phrase matters, not its spelling

parts.note: to bring home money is to earn it, as in bring home the bacon

explanation.surface: A vase you could grab to carry home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' looks like lifting the vase; it means catching a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a tall vase-shaped vessel, often with a foot, used for ashes or ornament.

clue.text: War captive sporting black eye? Victory could have been his?

indicators.note: a person sporting something wears it, so one part is shown inside the other

parts.note: a shiner is slang for a black eye
POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: A prisoner of war with a black eye might have been the winner?
explanation.walkthrough: Victory looks like a win in battle; it is Nelson's flagship HMS Victory, a vessel someone could own.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Victory was a ship, so whoever possessed such a vessel would be its proprietor in the shipping trade.

clue.text: Expert, long-serving royal polisher

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or expert, as in film buff
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the long-reigning Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: An experienced servant who has long polished for the royal household.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen; she reigned for seventy years, hence long-serving.
explanation.definitionFit: A buffer is a pad or wheel used to buff, that is to shine, a surface.

clue.text: Main network housed in room at the top

indicators.note: something housed in a place is kept inside it

parts.note: an attic is the room at the top of a house
a LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: The principal computer network is kept in the loft.
explanation.walkthrough: Main reads as an adjective meaning chief; in crosswords it is often the sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic term for the open ocean, and the Atlantic is one such ocean.

clue.text: Posh car emerging from pronounced gloom

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: murk is darkness or gloom

explanation.surface: A luxury car appears out of thick darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pronounced' looks like an adjective meaning marked, as in pronounced gloom; it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Merc is informal shorthand for a Mercedes, a prestige German motor vehicle.

clue.text: Dodgy French boarding house is freezing!

parts.note: sus is British slang for suspicious or dodgy
a pension is a French guesthouse

explanation.surface: A shady guesthouse in France turns out to be very cold!
explanation.walkthrough: Freezing seems to be about temperature; it means halting, as when payments or activities are frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension is a temporary halt, just as freezing a process stops it for a while.

clue.text: Card player before noon quiet — not up for port

parts.note: South is one of the four players at bridge
a.m. means before noon
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

indicators.note: in a down entry going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A card player rising before midday and keeping quiet is not getting up to go to the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: Southampton is a major English seaport on the south coast.

clue.text: Blue, having cut short dive — lacking this?

definitions.text: Blue, having cut short dive — lacking this?

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its final letter

parts.note: aqua is a greenish-blue colour
a dive or lunge is a sudden forward movement

explanation.surface: A diver turned blue in the face and cut the dive short — was the breathing gear missing?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a diver without breathing apparatus goes blue and must cut the dive short.
explanation.definitionFit: An aqualung is a diver's portable breathing apparatus, so lacking one ends a dive early.

clue.text: Old monarch's new name in doubt

indicators.note: in places one part inside another

parts.note: a query is a doubt or question

indicators.note: something new is remade, so these letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The name of a former king or queen is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes the 's, read as 'is': the old monarch is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Mary was a former English sovereign, such as Mary I or Mary II.

clue.text: Bone found in vegan lunch sent back

indicators.note: sent back means returned, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
found in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A bone turns up in a plant-based meal, which is returned to the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the human forearm.

clue.text: Forgiving person for telling tale?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who forgives or excuses
second meaning: a pilgrim in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales who tells a story

explanation.walkthrough: Telling tale suggests a snitch; it is a pilgrim who tells a story in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
explanation.definitionFit: A pardoner grants pardons, and The Pardoner's Tale is one of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Charity event possibly demanding payment: about time!

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a fee is a payment demanded for a service
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A fundraiser might ask for an entrance charge — and not before time!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' warns that the definition is an example: a fete is often held for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair, often held to raise money for good causes.

clue.text: School's staff mostly blunt about a head

indicators.note: about means surrounding one piece with another
mostly means not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: terse means curt or blunt
so much a head means so much each

explanation.surface: A school's staff are largely curt with the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: A head suggests the headteacher; it means per person, as in five pounds a head.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers are the instructing staff employed at a school.

clue.text: Civil engineer on climb becoming bright red

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer
a rise is a climb or ascent

explanation.surface: A civil engineer turns bright red on a steep ascent.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a vivid cherry-coloured shade of red.

clue.text: Dancing nude foxtrot, finished up exposed

indicators.note: dancing letters move around and come out rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to finish up is to end

explanation.surface: Someone dancing a nude foxtrot ended up rather exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Foxtrot looks like the dance; here it is the NATO alphabet's F.
explanation.definitionFit: Undefended means unprotected, open to attack, which is what exposed means.

clue.text: Complain when area's width is cut

parts.note: to moan is to complain
A is the abbreviation for area
W is the abbreviation for width

explanation.surface: A grumble about how wide the cut area of lawn is.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the middle as 'when A has W in its place': the letter for area is swapped out for the letter for width.
explanation.definitionFit: Mown is the past participle of mow, describing grass that has been cut.

clue.text: Wife with mechanical routine got down

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
rote is learning or doing things mechanically by repetition

explanation.surface: A wife's mechanical daily grind has left her depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Got down sounds like feeling low; it means putting words on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something down is to write it down, so got down is the past tense equivalent.

clue.text: Very fine polymath finally getting BA?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the preceding word

parts.note: the final letter of polymath
BA is British Airways, an airline

explanation.surface: A very bright polymath at last earns a Bachelor of Arts?
explanation.walkthrough: BA looks like a university degree, which a polymath might earn; it stands for British Airways.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline crack or margin is extremely thin, as narrow as a single hair.

clue.text: Wind up a piece of knitting

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a raised ridged band of stitches

explanation.walkthrough: Wind up suggests winding wool; in British slang to wind someone up is to tease them.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib is to tease playfully, and rib is also a ridged knitting stitch used for cuffs.

clue.text: Unacceptable to pinch one's idea

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: not on is an idiom for unacceptable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: It is not right to steal another person's idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is a British idiom meaning not acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a thought or conception, a synonym of idea.

clue.text: Extra Times edition's first for so long

parts.note: in cricket a bye is an extra, a run not scored off the bat
times as in multiplication, three by four

indicators.note: first says keep just the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of edition

explanation.surface: A special edition of The Times newspaper that has been a long time coming.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an extra is a run added to the score without being hit by the batter, and a bye is one kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye-bye and so long are both casual farewells said on parting.

clue.text: Betting caller will bring spaniel

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds at the start of a race
one who rings is a caller on the phone

explanation.surface: A bookie's caller will fetch the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the starting price, the odds on a horse when a race begins, a term from British racing.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is a breed of spaniel, used as a gun dog to flush game.
